post.summary: Receive a signed AI prediction callback
post.description: Accepts an AI prediction result as a durable receipt and queues asynchronous validation. The receipt boundary checks the JSON envelope, id, status, SUCCESS result object, and optional features array; it does not synchronously validate nested result fields. Nested result validation and optional persistence happen asynchronously and can later mark the receipt as errored. Both 202 and 200 acknowledge a durable receipt only. This endpoint uses custom HMAC request signing, not bearer authentication. Sign the exact raw HTTP request body bytes with HMAC-SHA256 over `timestamp + "." + nonce + "." + raw_body`; do not parse, reserialize, normalize, or otherwise change the bytes before signing. The timestamp must be fresh relative to the server clock; the production acceptance window is deployment-specific and is not stated in this contract. A nonce can be used only once: replaying the same nonce returns 409, while redelivering the same payload with a fresh nonce is idempotent and returns 200. Callback receipt ingestion is disabled by default until separately activated.

parameters.name: X-Mapilio-Timestamp
parameters.description: Required decimal Unix timestamp in seconds. It must be fresh relative to the server clock; the exact production acceptance window is deployment-specific.

parameters.name: X-Mapilio-Nonce
parameters.description: Required single-use request nonce.

parameters.name: X-Mapilio-Signature
parameters.description: HMAC-SHA256 digest as 64 hexadecimal characters, optionally prefixed with `sha256=`. This example is illustrative only and cannot be valid without the deployment signing secret.

202.description: A new callback receipt was durably stored and acknowledged for asynchronous validation. Nested result validation or persistence may later mark the receipt as errored.

200.description: The same payload was redelivered with a fresh nonce and matched an existing durable receipt. This acknowledgement is idempotent and does not synchronously validate nested result data. It is distinct from replaying a nonce, which returns 409.

401.description: The required signing headers are missing or invalid, the signature does not match the exact raw body, or the timestamp is not fresh.

409.description: The nonce has already been used. Sending the same payload with a fresh nonce is an idempotent duplicate and returns 200 instead.

413.description: The raw request body exceeds the configured callback payload limit.

422.description: The JSON is malformed, the top-level envelope, id, or status is invalid, SUCCESS lacks an object result, features is not an array when present, or the feature count exceeds the deployment-configured ceiling.

500.description: The callback receipt could not be stored or the accepted receipt could not be queued.

value.message: Callback receipt could not be stored.
Callback receipt could not be queued.

post.summary: Check whether the mobile email modal was shown
post.description: Accepts an empty POST body and preserves the exact behavior of legacy `POST /api/function/user_profile/profile/checkIsModalShown`. The first call for an authenticated user returns exactly `{status: false}` and atomically inserts one profile row; a repeat call returns exactly `{status: true}` without inserting another row. The endpoint uses the existing mobile bearer security boundary. The published contract contains no inactive/disabled-user exception serialization. No endpoint-specific throttle, response cache, ETag, or conditional request handling is part of this contract. The optional global API limiter may return the documented 429 response when deployment-configurable enforcement is enabled; production enforcement and its limits are not asserted by this contract.

post.description: Verifies the submitted email against the active mobile bearer user and returns a locally generated HMAC-SHA256 identity hash. No request body is required: an omitted body is accepted and returns the documented 401 failure when no email is available. Maintained mobile callers send `multipart/form-data` with the field `options[parameters][email]`; the runtime also accepts the equivalent JSON object `{options:{parameters:{email}}}`. Bearer lookup is controller-owned and requires an active mobile user; the email comparison is exact and case-sensitive. The success hash is lowercase hexadecimal and is synthetic in these examples. The signing key is selected from server-side configuration, using the configured OneSignal key with the mobile signing key as fallback; no key value is accepted from or returned to the caller. This endpoint performs no outbound OneSignal request. Missing, empty, wrong, or non-string-coerced email values and missing, invalid, stale, deleted, unactivated, or disabled bearer credentials use the versioned route's configured 401 failure status and exact generic error envelope. This contract documents only the versioned route and does not claim exact failure-status parity with its legacy counterpart. No endpoint-specific throttle, response cache, ETag, or conditional request handling is part of this contract, and no 304 response is defined. The deployment-optional global API limiter may return the documented 429 response when enforcement is enabled; it is not an endpoint-specific limiter, and production enforcement and limits are not asserted by this contract.

200.description: The email matched the active mobile bearer user and a synthetic local HMAC-SHA256 identity hash was returned.

401.description: The versioned route's configured generic failure response for missing, invalid, stale, deleted, unactivated, or disabled bearer credentials, or for missing, empty, wrong, or non-string-coerced email values. The exact legacy failure status is intentionally outside this versioned contract.

post.summary: Issue or refresh a public-client mobile bearer token
post.description: A shipped mobile application is a public client and does not send a client id or client secret. The password grant accepts either an email or username with a password; when both email and username are supplied, the current backend gives email precedence. The refresh_token grant exchanges a previously issued refresh token for a new bearer-token pair. Both application/json and multipart/form-data are accepted. Examples use synthetic credentials and tokens only.

post.summary: Sign out a mobile bearer session
post.description: Request validation runs before bearer lookup, so an invalid or oversized `refresh_token` returns 422 even without a bearer; the 401 cases below apply after request validation succeeds. A valid `Authorization: Bearer ...` mobile token is required. This route has only the shared `throttle:mobile-auth` middleware; bearer validation is controller-owned through `LegacyMobileAuth::userFromBearer`. Missing, invalid, stale, deleted-user, unactivated-user, and disabled-user bearer credentials all return the exact 401 envelope below. The optional `refresh_token` is a string with a maximum length of 4096 characters; explicit JSON null is accepted and treated as absent. An empty string is also treated as absent. A non-empty malformed or otherwise invalid signed refresh string that passes string and length validation is passed to `revokeToken`, whose false result is ignored; logout still succeeds. A valid supplied refresh token is recorded for revocation, as is the access token. The shared limiter selects its bucket from raw `grant_type` before controller validation: absent or any value other than exactly `refresh_token` uses the password/IP bucket, while raw `grant_type=refresh_token` uses the refresh/IP bucket even though `grant_type` is not a logout field. Revocation rows are recorded even when immediate denylist enforcement is disabled; the setting defaults to false, and a revoked token is rejected immediately only when `MAPILIO_MOBILE_AUTH_REVOCATION_ENABLED=true`. This endpoint has no endpoint-specific cache or ETag behavior and does not define a 304 response. Examples use synthetic token values only.

200.description: The bearer session was signed out. The access token is recorded for revocation, and a valid supplied refresh token is recorded too.

401.description: The controller could not resolve a valid active user from the bearer header. This includes a missing, invalid, stale, deleted-user, unactivated-user, or disabled-user bearer token.

422.description: The optional refresh_token failed request validation, such as being non-string or longer than 4096 characters. Validation runs before bearer lookup, so these requests return 422 even without a bearer. JSON null and an empty string are treated as absent; a non-empty syntactically malformed string that passes these rules is not a 422, is silently ignored by revocation, and logout returns 200.

example.message: The refresh token field must not be greater than 4096 characters.

refresh_token: The refresh token field must not be greater than 4096 characters.

message: Too many authentication attempts. Please try again later.

get.description: Returns the exact legacy-compatible `{data: {leaderboard: [...]}}` envelope. The versioned route uses sequence-point scoring and does not return pagination metadata. Each filter is optional; `user_id` restricts results to one positive user id, and `start_at` and `finish_at` define an inclusive date window only when both values are non-empty. Invalid user ids retain the legacy 400 envelope; an invalid complete date window uses the framework's standard 422 validation response. If the date values are reversed, the backend silently normalizes the window into chronological order. Unfiltered requests with none of `user_id`, `start_at`, or `finish_at` use the short-lived public aggregate cache; any of those query keys bypasses it, including an empty value. Legacy and versioned aliases share the same score-versioned cache semantics.

parameters.name: user_id
parameters.description: Optional positive integer user id. Supplying the key, including an empty value, bypasses the public aggregate cache.

parameters.name: start_at
parameters.description: Optional date-window start. Applied with finish_at when both values are non-empty; the backend normalizes the window to day boundaries. Supplying the key bypasses the public aggregate cache.

parameters.name: finish_at
parameters.description: Optional date-window end. Applied with start_at when both values are non-empty; the backend normalizes the window to day boundaries. Supplying the key bypasses the public aggregate cache.

200.description: The legacy-compatible leaderboard envelope. Numeric score and length values are decimal strings, not JSON numbers; roles may be null.

400.description: A non-empty user_id query value is not a positive integer.

422.description: A complete date window contains a value rejected by the backend date validator.

example.message: The start at field must be a valid date.

start_at: The start at field must be a valid date.

get.summary: Read the public imagery leaderboard winner status
get.description: Returns an unauthenticated, additive v1 alias of `GET /api/leaderboard-winner`. The supported query inputs are optional `user_id`, `start_at`, and `finish_at`. `user_id` is a positive int64 value forwarded on calculated responses and restricts the calculated leaderboard with the same public user filter as `GET /api/v1/imagery/leaderboard`; it has no effect on flags-only responses. The challenge window is inspected only when both date values are PHP-non-empty. If either date value is missing or empty, the exact response is `{data: {is_finished: false, is_calculated: false}}` and no leaderboard key is present. With both date values parseable, `is_finished` is true exactly when finish_at is earlier than the current server time. A matching non-deleted challenge with exact start and finish dates controls `is_calculated`; a missing table, row, or value defaults to false. When is_calculated is false, leaderboard is omitted. When it is true, leaderboard is the sequence-point scoring version 1 result, limited to at most 3 rows and using the same public `LeaderboardRow` schema, fields, and scalar types as `GET /api/v1/imagery/leaderboard`; a calculated empty result always contains `leaderboard: []`, while `is_finished` remains the boolean determined by finish_at. User-bearing row fields are existing public compatibility output; examples use synthetic values. No pagination metadata, server-side response cache, or ETag is part of this contract. The optional global API limiter may return the documented 429 response when deployment-configurable enforcement is enabled; production enforcement is not asserted by this contract.

parameters.name: user_id
parameters.description: Optional positive contributor id forwarded on calculated responses. It uses the same public user filter as `GET /api/v1/imagery/leaderboard` and has no effect on flags-only responses.

parameters.name: start_at
parameters.description: Optional challenge-window start string. The challenge window is inspected only when this and finish_at are both PHP-non-empty.

parameters.name: finish_at
parameters.description: Optional challenge-window finish string. The challenge window is inspected only when this and start_at are both PHP-non-empty.

200.description: The status-only or calculated public leaderboard-winner envelope. The conditional response shape is selected by the boolean data.is_calculated value.

get.description: Returns the unauthenticated v1 alias of `GET /api/get-types` and preserves its legacy response contract. The populated response is exactly `{data: [...], pagination: {...}}`; an empty or out-of-range page is exactly `{data: null}` with no pagination member. Rows are emitted in this order: `id`, `sort_order`, `created_at`, `created_by_id`, `updated_at`, `updated_by_id`, `deleted_at`, `code`, `group_id`, `icon`, `name`. Selected rows are non-deleted, so `deleted_at` is always null. IDs and nullable numeric metadata are JSON integers, timestamp strings use six fractional digits and a trailing `Z`, and code, icon, and name preserve string-or-null output. Ordering is ascending by id, except `code` equal to `end-of-pedestrians` uses synthetic sort 464.5, after id 464 and before id 465. The scalar `page` query value is PHP-int-cast and minimum-clamped to 1; omitted page is 1. The nonempty string `locale` is used, while an empty or non-string locale falls back to `en`; omitted locale uses the deployment application locale. Data fetching uses a limit and offset of 100, while legacy pagination reports `per_page` 15, 15-based page/link math, row-count-based `to`, and the total active row count. Pagination URLs and `path` always use `/api/get-types`, even for this v1 route, and preserve unrecognized or nested query keys through `http_build_query`; such keys, including `options[parameters][group_id]`, `options[paginate]`, and `per_page`, do not filter rows or change the fetch size. This contract does not define malformed array or extreme scalar page behavior. There is no endpoint authentication, response cache, or ETag. The optional global API limiter may return the documented 429 response when deployment-configurable enforcement is enabled; production enforcement and its limits are not asserted by this contract.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Optional scalar legacy page query value. It is PHP-int-cast and minimum-clamped to 1; omission uses 1. Malformed arrays and extreme values are outside this contract.

parameters.name: locale
parameters.description: Optional locale. A nonempty string is used; an empty or non-string value falls back to `en`, while omission uses the deployment application locale.

get.description: Returns the unauthenticated v1 alias of `GET /api/get-marketplaces` without changing the legacy response contract. The response is exactly `{data: {geojson: string}}`; `data.geojson` is a JSON-encoded string containing a GeoJSON FeatureCollection, not an object. Optional `lat` and `lon` query values are inspected with the legacy filled rules: coordinate validation and distance sorting activate only when both values are filled. A missing value, empty string, or exact query string `"0"` on either coordinate disables validation and sorting and emits `distance_km` as the string "0". Other filled query strings enter the active branch and must be numeric; active latitude must be in [-90, 90] and longitude in [-180, 180]. Numeric-distance rows are ordered ascending when available, but a missing-distance value and its placement are database-dependent: PostgreSQL can emit null when geometry is missing, while the portable path can retain the string "0" when geometry or its centroid is missing. The decoded inner object has `type: "FeatureCollection"` and `features` as an array or null when empty. Feature and property key order is part of the legacy JSON output; default PostgreSQL row ordering is not guaranteed. Text fields preserve nullable runtime output, `id` is an integer, and geometry is an object or null. No pagination metadata, response cache, or ETag is part of this contract. The optional global API limiter may return the documented 429 response when deployment-configurable enforcement is enabled; production enforcement is not asserted by this contract.

parameters.description: Optional legacy longitude query string. It participates in validation and distance sorting only when both lon and lat are legacy-filled; a missing value, empty string, or exact string "0" disables the coordinate branch.

get.description: Returns an unauthenticated, additive versioned alias of `GET /api/leaderboard-organization`. This operation consumes no query or path parameters. Unrelated query keys, including date, limit, pagination, and `score_version`-looking keys, are ignored; they do not alter the aggregate or bypass the shared cache. v1 uses sequence-point scoring version 1 and does not expose `score_version`. Legacy and versioned aliases share one score-versioned, configurable short-lived aggregate cache; disabling the cache bypasses existing cached values. The response is exactly `{data: {leaderboard: [...]}}`; an empty result is `{data: {leaderboard: []}}` and no pagination metadata is returned. Rows are ordered by point descending only; ties are unspecified. Row fields are emitted in this order: `organization_key`, `organization_name`, `point`, `total_length`, `total_images`. `organization_key` is a string, organization_name preserves string or null mapping, point and total_length are decimal strings when present, and total_images is an integer.

200.description: The exact public organization leaderboard envelope. Point and total length values are decimal strings when present; nullable mapped values remain null.

get.summary: Read a contributor's uploaded imagery groups
get.description: Returns the legacy mobile user-uploads feed through its versioned alias. Maintained mobile clients currently use `/api/user-uploads-v2`; this alias invokes the same controller and preserves its nested query names, row fields, nullability, and Laravel-style pagination object. The controller reads numeric `options[parameters][user_id]` values and integer-casts them, using the result when it is positive. It integer-casts scalar number/string values for `options[limit]` and `page`; an omitted limit defaults to 15, limit is then clamped to 1..1000, and page defaults to and is clamped to at least 1. Pagination link values intentionally retain the legacy `/api/user-uploads-v2` path, even when the request uses this versioned alias. Empty and out-of-range pages return `data: null` rather than an empty array.

parameters.name: options[parameters][user_id]

get.summary: Read a contributor's uploaded imagery details
get.description: Returns the unauthenticated v1 alias of `GET /api/user-uploads-detail-v2` with exact legacy JSON parity. The required nested scalar query values are `options[parameters][user_id]` and `options[parameters][group_key]`; missing `user_id` is reported before `group_key`. `user_id` must pass PHP `is_numeric`, is integer-cast with decimals truncated, and the result must be greater than zero. `group_key` rejects only null and the empty string, then scalar-casts to a string. `options[limit]` defaults to 15, is integer-cast, and is clamped to a minimum of 1 with no maximum; `page` defaults to 1, is integer-cast, and is clamped to a minimum of 1. Arrays, overflow, generic database failures, and invalid stored timestamps are outside this contract. Rows are selected from non-anomalous imagery joined to the requested group, ordered ascending by `imagery.id`, and contain exactly the documented eleven fields; there are no image URL, geometry, GeoJSON, organization, or project fields. `created_at` is formatted as a six-digit UTC ISO timestamp and `capture_time` as `Y-m-d H:i:s`, with nullable values preserved. A populated result is `{data: [...], pagination: {...}}`; an empty or out-of-range page is exactly `{data: null}`. Pagination is the legacy shape with `path` `/api/user-uploads-detail-v2`, `per_page` equal to the effective limit, and every URL built by re-encoding Laravel's parsed query keys with PHP `http_build_query` after overwriting `page`; nested `options` keys are serialized together before later top-level keys. The links contain Previous, a legacy bounded numeric/ellipsis window, and Next. Runtime bounds and performance, database indexes, duplicate joins, privacy/auth policy, clients and migration, and external services are outside this contract. There is no endpoint authentication, endpoint-specific response cache, or ETag.

get.summary: Read a user's public gamification badges
get.description: Returns the unauthenticated v1 alias of `GET /api/gamification/badges/{userId}` with exact success parity. `userId` is constrained only to numeric route values; a nonnumeric path does not match the route (the 404 body is not part of this contract). The optional `locale` query value is omitted by default and then uses the application locale; an empty value, array, or other non-string falls back to `en`. Scalar query strings are passed through verbatim, including unrecognized values; when no translation row matches, the source returns null translation fields and this contract claims no additional translation fallback. User existence checks only the id, so a row with a deleted timestamp remains visible in the badge and next-badge fields. The derived leaderboard lookup excludes deleted users, so this deleted-user branch returns `point` 0 and `next.percentage` `"0"`. A known user returns exactly `badges`, `point`, and `next`: badge metadata preserves enabled flags and legacy scalar values, timestamps are normalized to six-digit UTC ISO strings or null, and disabled badges may include a nested disabled image with file, disk, and folder metadata. `next.badge` is nullable and `next.percentage` preserves its string-or-integer legacy type. An unknown user returns HTTP 200 with the exact empty JSON array `[]`, not an object. There is no endpoint authentication, endpoint-specific throttle, response cache, ETag, or 304 behavior. If the optional global API limiter is enabled and enforced by deployment configuration, it may return the documented 429 envelope and headers.

PHP bracket syntax such as `locale[]=tr` is tolerated outside this canonical schema, parses as a non-string array, and falls back to `en`. Omission uses the application locale, an empty scalar falls back to `en`, and scalar strings (including unrecognized values) are passed through as-is.
